gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: There’s no rule against pushchairs, and in 2026 there was baby changing at each toilet bank. The park and ride buses only take a limited number of unfolded buggies, so I would bring one that folds.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: It’s a public area, so dogs aren’t banned, but the crowds are huge and the jets are extremely loud. You’re responsible for your dog’s safety, and only assistance animals are allowed in the Chill Out Zone, so I would leave yours at home if you can.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: You can bring your own food and drink, but BBQs and gas stoves aren’t allowed. The Low Green is an alcohol free zone apart from the bar area, so I would leave your own alcohol at home.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: Folding chairs and blankets are fine, but you’re asked not to bring tents or windbreaks, as they block the crowds and are a fire risk. Chairs, tables and awnings aren’t allowed in the car parks either.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: In 2026 there were drinking water stations around the festival site. I would bring a refillable bottle and fill it before the flying starts.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: There’s a Changing Places toilet with a hoist and a height adjustable bench next to the public toilets on the Low Green. RADAR toilets are at the Pavilion too.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: Entry is free, so there’s no carer ticket to buy. The two accessible viewing platforms take a disabled visitor plus one companion, first come first served.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything on hearing loops or BSL for the show. If you need either, I would ask the show before you go.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: In 2026 TLC Welfare had a quiet space in their marquee, on your right as you come in from Wellington Square. It’s worth knowing about if someone needs a break from the noise.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: There are no tickets for the seafront, so you can head into town and come back. The site does have a secured perimeter, so allow a little time to get back in when it’s busy.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: Any steward or police officer can point you to first aid. Free wristbands for children were given out at the Destination South Ayrshire marquees and by the police in 2026, and found children go to the welfare points, so agree a meeting point too as phone signal can be poor.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. The Chill Out Zone is only partly under cover, and there were no refunds for rain.

ground.html:
The Ground Show

The Festival Village fills the Low Green right behind the crowd line. I gave a quick idea of it in the , so here’s the detail. In 2026 it opened two hours before the Friday flying and an hour and a half before the Saturday flying, which is plenty of time if you get there early.

EntryFree
Friday16:00 to 21:00
Saturday12:00 to 18:00
FunfairUntil 21:30 Fri, 19:30 Sat

How I Would Do It

  1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat, head to the Esplanade railings and set up your chairs or blanket before anything else.
  2. Then walk the villageTake a look round the Military Village, speak to the crews, visit the trade stalls and check the food options while someone minds your spot. It gets very busy once the crowds arrive.
  3. Toilet before the flyingI would go before the first display. In 2026 that was the Red Arrows at 18:10 on the Friday and the Red Devils at about 13:35 on the Saturday.
  4. Use the gapsIf you aren’t waiting for a particular display, use it as a toilet or food break, or pop back to the village.

Things To See And Do

Both days

The Military Village

The RAF, Army and Navy are all on the Low Green, with personnel on hand to answer your questions about life in the forces. If anyone in your group is thinking about joining up, this is the place to ask.

Saturday (2026)

The Static Helicopter

In 2026 the static display was a Belgian Air Force Agusta A109BA on the Low Green on the Saturday. It’s a small static show, as it’s a seafront event. If an aircraft is opened up for you to take a look inside, it’s worth a peek, and some crews sell exclusive merch in or outside the aircraft.

Friday (2026)

The Falcons Landing

The RAF Falcons parachute display finished in the landing zone on the Low Green in 2026. Children love to see them come down right by the village.

Free to look

Exhibitions

Solway Aviation Museum, the Scottish Aeromodellers Association, the Royal Highland Fusiliers Museum and the Scottish Fire Brigade Heritage Trust were there in 2026, plus classic car and motorcycle clubs and a Spitfire themed Jaguar XJ.

Both days

Red Arrows Simulator

If you’ve ever wondered what it’s like to fly a jet, this is your chance. I would get to it early, before the queues build.

Both days

Zip Line And Drone Soccer

The zip line was new in 2026, and so was the drone soccer arena, where children steer drone balls inside a netted cage.

Both days

The Family Zone

Laser tag, zorb bubble football, mini bikes, mini Highland Games, a magic show, a dinosaur show, a circus workshop and library and museum activities, when I last checked. That should keep little ones busy until the flying.

Both days

Cosmos Planetarium

A dome planetarium showing “Capcom Go! The Apollo Story” in 2026. It may work for you as a calm sit down if the noise outside gets a bit much.

Both days

The STEM Village

Hands on science, technology, engineering and maths activities, with people from the industry to talk to. A good one for curious kids who want to know how the aircraft work.

Programme £5 (2026)

Trade Village And Merch

Local traders sell their goods in the Ayrshire Trade Village, and there are merchandise and programme stands with Ayr Show branded goods. The RAF Benevolent Fund, the show’s charity partner, has a marquee too.

For the food village, the bar and the toilets, take a look at . If you’re hoping to meet the Red Arrows pilots, the 2026 times are in the .

Jack’s tipEar defenders aren’t handed out at Ayr, so bring your own. Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible, as the Typhoon is very loud along the Esplanade. There’s no cash machine on site either, so I would bring a little cash in case the card machines lose signal.

skipped.flights: I couldn't find any pleasure, helicopter, warbird or balloon flights offered at or from the show. It's a seafront show with no airfield, and the official pages don't mention any.
skipped.support: The show is free and run by South Ayrshire Council. There are no public donation, bucket collection or volunteer appeals; the only ask is business sponsorship by email, plus the RAF Benevolent Fund marquee as the event charity partner, which is mentioned briefly in the ground show instead.

The FAQs advise not bringing tents and windbreaks, as they restrict crowd movement and are a fire risk. 4) Food and facilities, What can I bring?, says the alcohol rules couldn't be found.
